items.summary: दिल्ली की सड़कों पर आज पुलिस पूरी तरह धरपकड़ के मूड में नजर आई. प्रदर्शनकारियों से लेकर पत्रकारों तक सबको एक सिरे से उठाया गया. साथ ही रिपोर्टिंग के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाले फोन जब्त किए गए. इस तरह आज का दिन बड़े पैमाने पर हिरासत की कार्रवाई के नाम रहा. गौरतलब है कि मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफ़े की मांग और चुनाव आयोग की ओर से जारी विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण के विरोध में होने वाले प्रदर्शन से पहले जंतर-मंतर तक पहुंचने के रास्तों पर बैरिकेडिंग कर दी गई थी और भारी संख्या में पुलिस बल तैनात था. दिल्ली आ रहे लोगों ने ट्रेनों में हिरासत में लिए जाने की बात कही, वहीं बसों के रास्ते बदले गए और छात्रों को प्रदर्शन में शामिल न होने की चेतावनी दिए जाने की खबरें भी सामने आईं. मौके पर रिपोर्टिंग कर रहे न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री के पत्रकारों को भी हिरासत में लिया गया और उनके काम के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाले फोन जब्त कर लिए गए. घंटों बाद उन्हें रिहा किया गया, लेकिन इस अपडेट के समय तक दूसरे पत्रकार और यूट्यूबर्स हिरासत में थे. ऐसे में बड़ा सवाल यही है कि अगर आप प्रदर्शन स्थल तक पहुंच ही नहीं सकते, तो विरोध करने के अधिकार का क्या मतलब रह जाता है? और जब पत्रकारों को भी हिरासत में लेकर बसों में बैठा दिया जाए, तो वे आपको वहां की स्थिति कैसे दिखाएंगे? राजधानी में पुलिस की व्यापक कार्रवाई के दिन की हमारी ग्राउंड रिपोर्ट्स देखिए. जंतर-मंतर प्रदर्शन की कवरेज कर रहे न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री के तीन पत्रकार और इंटर्न हिरासत में, फोन भी छीने, बाद में छोड़ा जंतर-मंतर प्रदर्शन: किले में तब्दील हुई राजधानी, हजारों सुरक्षाकर्मी तैनात और रेल-मेट्रो पर लगी रोक

items.title: Delhi’s Detention Day: Protesters picked up, journalists detained
items.summary: People picked up from the streets. Journalists detained. Reporting phones seized. Delhi’s October 10 protest became a day of sweeping detentions. Ahead of the protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation and opposing SIR, access to Jantar Mantar was choked by layers of barricades and heavy police deployment. People travelling towards Delhi reported being detained on trains, while buses were diverted and students warned against attending. On the ground, Newslaundry reporters were detained and their work phones seized. They have since been released, but other journalists and YouTubers remained in detention at the time of this update. items.title: Asking questions to minister not defamation; Parvesh Verma approached court with unclean hands: Delhi court
items.summary: A Delhi court on Saturday observed that in a democracy, it is the right of the press and public to ask questions to the government, and the government and elected official must listen to opinions which are different from their own. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Neha Mittal of the Rouse Avenue Courts said that a merely asking questions to representative of public in parliament regarding any law and order situation or any other matter, cannot amount to defamation. "Any contrary view will rather be a dark spell in the era of democracy paving way for utter disregard of the constitutional rights," the Court underscored. Judge Mittal made the observation while rejecting the criminal defamation case filed by Delhi Deputy Chief Minister Parvesh Verma against Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Saurabh Bharadwaj over certain social media posts made by the latter. The Court refused to take cognisance of the case, holding that Bharadwaj's posts were in the nature of questions asked with the purpose of criticising the government and not to defame anyone. items.title: Men received 70% of arbitrator appointments across the Supreme Court, Delhi and Bombay HCs: MKBAC study at NALSAR
items.summary: Men received 70% of recorded arbitrator appointments made by the Supreme Court, Delhi High Court and Bombay High Court, according to a study by NALSAR University of Law. The study found that of the 2,283 appointments for which gender information was recorded, 1,598 appointments, or 70.03%, went to men, while only 685 appointments, or 29.97%, went to women. The disparity was consistent across all three courts, with men accounting for 79.17% of recorded appointments at the Supreme Court, 71.30% at the Bombay High Court and 68.88% at the Delhi High Court. The findings form part of a report titled Arbitrator Appointments in Numbers , prepared by the Milon K Banerji Centre for Arbitration Law at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad. The Centre is chaired by former Supreme Court Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman , with Senior Advocate Ritin Rai serving as Co-Chair and Advocate Dr. Amit George as Director (Research). Senior Advocate Gourab Banerji is its Donor and Patron, while Advocates Shreya Parikh and Chand Chopra serve as Associate Directors (Research). The report examined 3,688 cases registered in 2025 before the three courts, with data collected until June 30, 2026. The researchers observed that the composition of the arbitrator pool reflected a substantial gender imbalance, alongside a concentration of appointments among advocates and retired judges. Of the appointments for which professional backgrounds were recorded, 73.21% went to advocates, 23.73% to retired judges and only 3.10% to technical experts. The Supreme Court displayed a markedly different pattern, with retired judges accounting for 88% of its recorded appointments. However, the researchers cautioned that the Supreme Court dataset was relatively small. Technical experts accounted for just 1.43% of appointments in Bombay and 4.14% in Delhi. The researchers recommended that courts and arbitral institutions broaden their pools of eligible arbitrators. The report said, " The disparity in the appointments on the basis of gender are particularly concerning and need to be addressed ." They also suggested including more qualified technical experts, particularly in disputes involving specialised sectors such as construction and infrastructure. Few arbitrators receive repeated appointments Apart from the gender imbalance, the study revealed that a small group of arbitrators received a disproportionate share of appointments. items.title: Delhi court says Sharjeel Imam violated interim bail condition by interacting with media
items.summary: A Delhi court on Saturday said that Sharjeel Imam violated his interim bail condition in the Delhi riots conspiracy case by interacting with the media. However, Additional Sessions Judge Sameer Bajpai of Karkardooma courts said he was not cancelling Imam's bail since he has to surrender by today evening. The Court had granted Imam bail for seven days from October 4 to October 10 to attend the wedding functions of his cousin brothers. One of the conditions imposed in the interim bail order was that Imam must not come in contact with the media or use social media. Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) Madhukar Pandey appeared for the prosecution and argued that Imam violated this condition. He relied on videos uploaded on YouTube and social media platform X to argue that Imam was present in a room when his brother gave an interview to news agency ANI. Pandey also referred to the ANI videos in which Sharjeel Imam was sitting in his living room, talking to people present in the room. Pandey said that such a video could not have been shot without Imam’s knowledge. Advocate Talib Mustafa appeared for Imam and contended that he had neither interacted with any journalist nor given an interview. He stated that the video uploaded by News 24 was a compilation of separate clips and that the interview was given by Imam's brother, who was not bound by the bail conditions. After watching the videos, the court rejected the defence's contention that Imam was not present when the interview was recorded. The court noted that the clips showed Imam and several other people in the same room where his brother was being interviewed. It further observed that the relevant portions of the video bore ANI's identification, indicating that they were recorded by the same media organisation. “Thus, it is clear that not only the first part of the video, in which the brother of the accused was giving interview to the media person, but the second part and the third part also were shot by the same media person of ANI News. Apparently these facts and circumstances show that the media person of the ANI News was there in the same room where the accused was also sitting. Thus, apparently the accused has flouted the term ii of the bail order dated 22.09.2026, whereby he was granted interim bail,” the Court said. However, it said that since Imam has to surrender today, it will not be appropriate to cancel his interim bail. Imam has been in jail since January 2020 after he was booked in a number of cases

items.title: Delhi Riots: Court convicts Tahir Hussain for abetment
items.summary: A Delhi court on Saturday convicted former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) councillor Tahir Hussain of the offence of abetment to rioting in a case related to Delhi riots. Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh of the Karkardooma Court acquitted Hussain of all other offences. The Court also acquitted co-accused Md Shadab, Shah Alam, Riyasat Ali, Gulfam, Md Rihan, Arshad Qayyum and Irshad Ahmed of all the charges. A detailed order is awaited. The FIR in the case was registered under Sections 147, 148, 149, 427, 436, 120B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) at Dayalpur police station. One Irshad Ali had filed the complaint alleging that his shop was looted and set on fire on February 24, 2020, causing losses of ₹17–18 lakh in stolen goods and ₹10 lakh in property damage. Another complainant, Mohd Zahid, said rioters raised slogans in support of Tahir Hussain, whom two constables identified during the investigation. Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) Madhukar Pandey appeared for the State. Tahir Hussain was represented through advocate Rajiv Mohan.

items.title: Supreme Court dismisses lawyer’s plea seeking listing of 21 cases before Madras High Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed an advocate’s plea challenging a Madras High Court order rejecting his plea for listing of 21 pending cases filed by him on behalf of his clients [LK Charles Alexander v. Registrar General, Madras High Court]. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath , Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh declined to interfere with the High Court’s decision. “ The registry works under the orders of whom? Tell us. Have you ever seen what the cause list says at the end? Published under the orders of the Chief Justice. You want a direction to the Chief Justice. Dismissed, ” Justice Nath said. Advocate LK Charles Alexander told the Court that he had filed a writ petition before the High Court seeking directions for the listing of the cases pending there. “ You filed a writ of mandamus before the High Court to direct other courts to take up your matters? ” Justice Nath asked. “ To direct the registry, My Lords, ” Alexander clarified. Justice Nath then asked whether Alexander was a lawyer. After he answered in the affirmative, the Court dismissed his plea. Justice Sandeep Mehta, Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh Alexander had approached the Madras High Court alleging that 21 cases filed by him on behalf of his clients had not been listed despite repeated requests to the registry. On July 3, a division bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan dismissed his petition, holding that writ petitions could not be used to bypass established listing procedures. The High Court said that lawyers and litigants had no vested or fundamental right to have their matters listed ahead of earlier-filed cases, except by following the prescribed procedure for seeking urgent listing. It pointed out that Alexander could submit a mention memo before the bench handling the relevant roster or make a representation to the Registrar (Judicial) regarding any listing discrepancies. Alexander subsequently challenged the judgment before the Supreme Court. The High Court held that lawyers and litigants cannot use writ petitions to bypass established listing procedures. pic.twitter.com/ctfG0gQs7s — Bar and Bench (@barandbench) October 9, 2026

items.title: What is good for the goose is good for the gander
items.summary: Recently, former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai criticised sitting Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan for the latter's public remarks on the right to vote. In a speech delivered on October 4 , Justice Bhuyan had said that any process which disenfranchises millions of Indian citizens is intrinsically arbitrary and a negation of the constitutional order. No "whataboutery" can justify the act of taking away voting rights of citizens, he said. "If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India." He added, "Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens making them citizens without voting rights would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of the Constitution of India." He made it clear that no institution was exempt. "No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution," he declared. On the deletion of names from electoral rolls, Justice Bhuyan was categorical. "Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing. From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body." items.title: Meghalaya High Court initiates suo motu case against Shillong bar bodies for strike against Advocate General
items.summary: The Meghalaya High Court has issued contempt of court notice to the officer bearers of Shillong Bar Association and the High Court of Meghalaya Bar Association for calling for suspension of judicial work to demand the removal of Advocate General Amit Kumar. The Bar bodies have been seeing Kumar's removal on account of his statement in a case that the bar has failed to protect the women lawyers in the State. Taking objection to the same, the bar bodies asked lawyers to abstain from judicial work from October 1 till the State accedes to their demand for Kumar's removal. A bench of Chief Justice Revati Mohite Dere and Justice HS Thangkhiew on October 1 initiated a suo motu public interest litigation (PIL), taking judicial cognizance of the ongoing strike of lawyers in the High Court and all districts except Baghmara district. It noted that the law is settled that lawyers have no right to go on strike or even token strike or to give a call for strike. Thus, the Court opined that the strike called by the bar bodies amounts to obstruction of administration of justice. "Considering that the call for abstention given by the Shillong Bar Association and the High Court of Meghalaya Bar Association has obstructed administration of justice, the same would constitute criminal contempt under Section 2(c) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971," it said. The matter will be heard on October 13. "All contemnors to personally remain present on the next date. Contempt notices be served through the Registrar General, High Court of Meghalaya to enable the contemnors to appear before this Court," the Court directed. The Court said if judicial work is not resumed by the advocates in other districts, it will be constrained to issue contempt notices even against the President, Secretary and office bearers of the district bar associations. items.title: Nation has been driven back: Supreme Court laments its own 1987 judgment on condonation of delay
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed displeasure over its own 1987 judgment in Collector, Land Acquisition v. Katiji , observing that the decision, which condoned a delay of merely four days, had driven the country backwards because litigants have since repeatedly relied on it to seek condonation of delay. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu made the observation while dismissing appeals filed by Karvy Stock Broking Limited and its former Chairman and Managing Director C Parthasarathy against Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) orders refusing to condone delays in challenging penalties imposed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). " Our nation has been driven back because of the decision in 1987, when for condoning a delay of only four days, this Court wrote about 15–16 pages. And that is the decision in Collector, Land Acquisition v. Katiji, which has now been used so long as if this is the panacea for all ills in condonation of delay applications ," the Bench remarked. In its 1987 judgment, the Supreme Court advocated a liberal approach to condonation of delay, holding that substantial justice should prevail over technical considerations. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu The Court observed that the judgment had subsequently been treated as a general justification for condoning delays in legal proceedings. It also referred to subsequent Supreme Court judgments, including Sheo Raj Singh , and emphasised that different considerations apply when a court itself exercises discretion to condone delay and when an appellate court reviews another forum's exercise of discretion. It also clarified that regulatory authorities and private litigants would be treated equally in matters involving delayed appeals. items.title: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court to hear plea to allow excluded voters under appeal to vote for upcoming municipal elections

items.title: Delhi High Court refuses urgent hearing in Youth Congress petition for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to allow urgent listing of a petition filed by Indian Youth Congress (IYC) challenging the Delhi Police' refusal to permit them to hold a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. The plea filed by IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib was mentioned before acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre by Senior Advocate Sanjoy Ghose . Ghose said that he had mentioned the matter yesterday too and the Court had granted him liberty to mention the matter today if it is not listed. "What is the urgency? We will hear it on Monday," Justice Sambre said. Chib has challenged the Delhi Police’s order of October 1 rejecting their application. According to the plea, the IYC had applied on September 25 seeking permission to hold a peaceful demonstration involving around 100-150 people. The organisation said it had undertaken to comply with all lawful conditions relating to security, traffic management, discipline and maintenance of public order. The plea states that despite repeated follow-ups, the police communicated the rejection only on October 1, which was also the first proposed date of the demonstration. According to the petition, the power of the police to regulate assemblies does not extend to imposing a blanket prohibition without an individualised and proportionate assessment of the circumstances. As per the plea, the decision by the police amounts to a violation of fundamental rights to freedom of speech and expression and peaceful assembly under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. The plea has challenged the "mechanical application" of guidelines governing protests and assemblies. The plea was filed through advocate Roopesh Singh Bhadauria. items.title: Digital arrest scam: Bombay High Court denies bail to accused whose bank account received ₹4 crore
items.summary: The Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court recently rejected the anticipatory bail plea of an accused whose bank account was credited with ₹4.03 crore in a ₹7.17 crore digital arrest cyber fraud case [Anuj Saxena v. State & Anr.] Justice RM Joshi held that custodial interrogation of the accused is essential to investigate such cyber crimes and identify the real culprits. Justice RM Joshi (Bombay HC) The case arose from a first information report (FIR) registered in Maharashtra where a doctor was pressured into paying ₹7.17 crore under a digital arrest scam. Investigation revealed that ₹4.03 crore of the defrauded sum was credited directly to the account of the accused, one Anuj Saxena, and subsequently withdrawn. Saxena claimed he ran a charitable institution and shared his bank details to receive a promised ₹20 lakh donation. He further alleged his phone was hacked. However, the Court found no evidence on record to support his hacking defense. Justice Joshi highlighted the severity of digital arrest frauds as he rejected the anticipatory bail prayed by Saxena. “The offence in question is serious in nature. Needless to say that there is increase in the number of persons being defrauded by digital arrests,” the Court observed. The judge warned against accepting unverified explanations from account holders. “Any frivolous or afterthought explanation by the persons whose accounts are credited with crime money would amount to lend encouragement to commission of such crimes,” the bench stated. The court concluded that custodial interrogation in such cases is absolutely necessary in order to investigate into the crime and find perpetrators and real culprits. Advocate PR Dubey appeared for Saxena. Additional public prosecutor RP Gour appeared for State. items.title: Kerala High Court comes to aid of principal denied entry to school for wearing churidar
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently directed the police to ensure that a headmistress of a high school in Kottarakkara is allowed to enter the educational institution freely after she was allegedly stopped at the gate for wearing a churidar [Sindhu S Nair v Secretary, General Education Department & ors] Justice PV Kunhikrishnan said that a person's choice of attire cannot be dictated by another person or by societal customs unless such a restriction has the backing of law. The Court emphasised that when such dictates are issued against the individual choices of a citizen, it is the duty of the law-enforcing authority to take appropriate legal steps. " What dress one wears is ordinarily a matter of personal choice of every citizen of this country. No one or society as a whole can dictate how a citizen should dress without the backing of the law. This is a part of the fundamental rights of every citizen, " the Court said. It added that clothes are an expression of culture, comfort, and individual choice which cannot be used to measure a person's worth or dignity. The Court declared that a citizen's attire is her choice and cannot be restricted by any societal customs. " I declare that a citizen's attire is his/her choice, and nobody can insist that it conform to society's customs, nor can anybody dictate that it be in a manner acceptable to society, especially when no law backs it." Justice PV Kunhikrishnan Though the dispute appears to be a simple issue of whether a headmistress could wear a churidar instead of a saree during working hours, it raises broader questions concerning the dignity and autonomy of a woman, the Court SAID. " The Constitution does not make a woman's dignity contingent on her conformity with another person’s preferred mode of attire. Dress is a personal choice ," it added. The Court further emphasised that the dignity or cultural significance attached to an attire is for the person wearing it to decide and cannot be imposed according to societal preferences. " No one can restrict it, and no one can dictate which dress an individual must wear. The dignity and cultural tradition of an attire should be decided by the person concerned, not by society, " the Court said. items.title: Actor Imran Khan, activist Tushar Gandhi among 400 detained at Mumbai protest
items.summary: Actor Imran Khan and activist Tushar Gandhi were among those detained in Mumbai on Saturday, October 10, as police moved to prevent demonstrations in support of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest in Delhi. More than 400 people were detained across Mumbai, according to an India Today report . At least 200 of them were picked up at August Kranti Maidan, where a gathering had been planned to express solidarity with protesters in Delhi. The Mumbai demonstration was called amid the CJP’s demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities and concerns about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Mumbai Police had refused permission for the gathering. Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi and head of the organisation Hum Bharat Ke Log, was detained while travelling to August Kranti Maidan. The Indian Express reported that he was taken from Bandra to the DN Nagar police station. Activist Feeroz Mithiborwala was also detained at his residence and taken to the MIDC police station, India Today reported. Members of Hum Bharat Ke Log and supporters of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) were among those detained at August Kranti Maidan. Police action extended to other parts of the city. Workers of the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA), led by Prakash Ambedkar, were detained while demonstrating near Hutatma Chowk in south Mumbai. Additional police personnel were deployed at August Kranti Maidan and Shivaji Park, while barricades were erected to prevent gatherings. Rubaid Bhojani, one of the protesters, alleged that the police had detained demonstrators “very brutally”, according to India Today. The detentions in Mumbai came as authorities in Delhi stepped up security ahead of the proposed CJP demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The party has accused the Election Commission of electoral irregularities and raised concerns about voter deletions during the SIR exercise. It has demanded that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign. Delhi Police denied permission for the demonstration, citing procedural issues and concerns over public safety and law and order. Several protesters and student leaders were detained at different locations as police attempted to prevent people from gathering in the capital.
